name: Liposuction-assisted mastectomy

card.summary: A gynecomastia operation that combines liposuction of fatty tissue with surgical removal of the breast gland to give men a flatter, more masculine chest contour.
card.note: Surgical procedure with recognised complications such as hematoma, seroma and contour irregularity.

quick.overview:
Liposuction-assisted mastectomy treats male breast enlargement (gynecomastia) by pairing two techniques: liposuction removes fatty tissue and mastectomy removes the firm glandular tissue under the nipple. Together they aim at a flat, defined chest.

It is described as a surgical option when gynecomastia persists and medication has not resolved it. The American Board of Cosmetic Surgery is cited as calling surgery the most effective known treatment for the condition.
quick.how: The procedure is performed by a surgeon under anaesthesia; the removed gland is routinely sent for pathology. Surgeons typically choose technique by grade, with more skin excess calling for additional measures. Adolescents are generally advised to wait until puberty is complete.
quick.risks: Reported complications of mastectomy include hematoma, infection, asymmetry, altered sensation, nipple or areola necrosis, seroma, noticeable scars and contour deformities. Many US insurers treat it as cosmetic and do not cover it.

lead: Liposuction-assisted mastectomy is a combined surgical treatment for gynecomastia, the benign enlargement of male breast tissue. It joins liposuction, which reduces fat, with subcutaneous mastectomy, which removes glandular tissue.[1]
It is used to flatten and sculpt the male chest, so that clothing sits better and the pectoral area looks more masculine, and is often discussed in the hardmaxxing category of looksmaxxing.

Surgery is typically considered when gynecomastia lasts more than about 12 months, causes distress, and has reached a fibrotic stage that does not respond to medication; in adolescents it is generally postponed until puberty is complete.[1]

chain: Gland excision removes firm breast tissue
angle.text: The operation directly reduces the volume that creates a feminine chest profile, which people undergo to improve how they look in and out of clothing.

paras: Gynecomastia is graded in four stages, with grade I and II lacking excess skin and grade III and IV involving skin excess; skin excess is the feature that separates lower from higher grades.[1] Alongside liposuction-assisted mastectomy, Wikipedia lists subcutaneous mastectomy, laser-assisted liposuction and laser lipolysis without liposuction as surgical options.[1]
In the combined approach the fat is suctioned and the glandular disc is excised, and the tissue is routinely examined in pathology to confirm the diagnosis and check for tumours.[1]
In 2019, 24,123 men had gynecomastia surgery in the US, 19% more than in 2000, and 60% of patients were under 29. The average surgeon's fee was $4,123.[1]
Complications listed for mastectomy include hematoma, wound infection, asymmetry, sensation changes, nipple or areola necrosis, seroma, painful or visible scars and contour deformities.[1]
